anchor.statement: Lemma B.7. Fix the data for the outer profile and the axis, Λ , and a finite parameter order k. Put ℓ i = log(CE(X i , η )) and G i = U(X i , η ). Let ω fin be the sum of the logarithmic radial lengths of the final axial cutoff and the interpolation of a to .8 in the proof of Proposition B.5. The continuations constructed there satisfy ∥ℓ i ∥ C k η ≤ B k , ∥G i − U ∗ ∥ Ck η ≤ C nat k Λ + C join k ( Λ )(t 1 + κ0 + ω fin ). (B.32) The constant C nat k is independent of both Λ and sufficiently large C, with the preceding axis data fixed. The bounds B k and C join k ( Λ ) may depend on Λ , but are independent of sufficiently large C and of smaller radial transition widths.

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: The envelope theorem states (B.32) for all derivative orders up to a given N, with Cnat chosen before Λ and B, Cjoin after Λ, uniformly in the amplitude and widths (ω_fin written as w1 + w2, t1 as T, κ0 as κ); the second declaration identifies endpointLog with log(C E(110, η)).
